description: Action library for bimanual hand gesture recognition pipeline. Grounded in HandX (CVPR 2026) kinematic feature taxonomy, biomechanics literature (Frontiers in Neurorobotics 2021), and quantitative grasp taxonomy (JNR 2019). 36 classes across three movement scales.

schema_notes.id_format: SCALE_NNN where SCALE is MIC (micro), MAC (macro), or BIM (bimanual)
schema_notes.contact_ratio_range: Estimated [min, max] from HandX compute_contact_metric.py. Calibrate against actual video data using: python src/annotator.py --calibrate --json_file outputs/json/video01.json
schema_notes.handx_kinematic_signal: Feature extracted by HandX annotate_single.py that most reliably triggers this class

scale_thresholds.micro: contact_ratio <= 0.25 — isolated finger articulations, no sustained inter-hand contact
scale_thresholds.macro: 0.05 <= contact_ratio <= 0.45 — wrist/arm-dominant gestures, single hand primary
scale_thresholds.bimanual: contact_ratio >= 0.30 AND both hands detected — coordinated two-hand operations

action_library.label: fingertip_pinch
action_library.description: Thumb tip and index tip make contact; remaining fingers extended. Highest-precision grasp used for small object manipulation.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: thumb-index fingertip distance < 0.02m, other fingertip distances > 0.04m
action_library.notes: Distinguished from lateral_pinch by tip-to-tip vs pad-to-side contact geometry

action_library.label: lateral_pinch
action_library.description: Thumb pad presses against the lateral surface of the index finger mid-phalanx; no fingertip-to-fingertip contact. Used for flat object manipulation.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: thumb pad to index PIP lateral distance < 0.02m, index tip free
action_library.notes: Key distinction from MIC_001: contact is at mid-phalanx not fingertip

action_library.label: tripod_pinch
action_library.description: Thumb, index, and middle fingertips converge to a single point. Used for pen-like, needle, or small tool manipulation.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: three-fingertip cluster radius < 0.025m simultaneously
action_library.notes: Requires all three tips to be within threshold simultaneously — stricter than MIC_001

action_library.label: index_point
action_library.description: Index finger fully extended, remaining fingers curled into palm. No inter-finger contact. Pointing or directing gesture.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: index flexion ratio < 0.1, middle/ring/pinky flexion ratio > 0.7
action_library.notes: Low contact_ratio because no finger-to-finger contact; distinguished by selective extension pattern

action_library.label: finger_extension
action_library.description: One or more fingers moving from a flexed to a fully extended position. Open-hand or spreading motion. Flexion ratio decreasing over the chunk window.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: finger flexion ratio decreasing event on one or more fingers over time
action_library.notes: Temporal class — requires change over time, not a static posture

action_library.label: finger_flexion
action_library.description: One or more fingers curling from extended toward the palm. Closing motion without reaching full-power grasp.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: finger flexion ratio increasing event on one or more fingers over time
action_library.notes: Complement of MIC_005. If all fingers flex together to full closure, prefer MAC_006 power_grasp

action_library.label: finger_adduction
action_library.description: Fingers moving toward the hand midline — inter-finger spacing decreasing, fingers converging parallel.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: inter-finger abduction angle decreasing at MCP joints
action_library.notes: Watch for finger-to-finger contact at low inter-finger distances

action_library.label: finger_abduction
action_library.description: Fingers spreading away from the hand midline — fan-out motion of extended fingers.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: inter-finger abduction angle increasing at MCP joints
action_library.notes: Complement of MIC_007; zero contact_ratio expected as fingers move apart

action_library.label: thumb_opposition
action_library.description: Thumb rotating across the palm to oppose a specific finger; high rotational component at the CMC joint. Foundational motion for all pinch grasps.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: thumb CMC rotation event combined with palm-crossing trajectory
action_library.notes: Distinguished from MIC_001/002/003 by the rotational path rather than final contact state

action_library.label: thumb_extension
action_library.description: Thumb moving away from the palm into an extended or abducted position; no contact with other fingers.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: thumb flexion ratio decreasing event, thumb-finger distances increasing
action_library.notes: Complement of thumb_opposition; signals preparation for a grasp or a communicative gesture (thumbs-up)

action_library.label: in_hand_rotation
action_library.description: Object or fingers rotating within the grasp of one hand using primarily finger and thumb movements; wrist remains relatively static.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: high finger flexion variability over time, low wrist linear velocity
action_library.notes: Key discriminator from MAC_001/002: wrist velocity must remain low for this to be micro, not macro

action_library.label: finger_tapping
action_library.description: Rapid repeated contact and release of a single fingertip against a surface, thumb, or other fingertip. High contact frequency, short contact duration per event.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: contact_frequency > 2.0 Hz, avg_contact_duration < 0.15s
action_library.notes: Only class where contact_frequency is the primary discriminator rather than contact_ratio

action_library.label: power_curl
action_library.description: All four fingers flexing simultaneously into the palm without thumb involvement. Grip-closing motion in isolation from the thumb.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: simultaneous flexion increase across all four finger chains, thumb remains static
action_library.notes: Distinguished from MAC_006 power_grasp by absence of thumb involvement and lower wrist velocity

action_library.label: static_hold_precision
action_library.description: Hand maintaining a stable precision posture (e.g., pen hold, tool grip) with minimal finger movement for at least one second.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: low flexion ratio variance over full chunk window, contact_ratio stable
action_library.notes: Temporal class requiring stability — high variance in flexion over the window disqualifies this label

action_library.label: wrist_pronation
action_library.description: Forearm rotating so the palm faces downward from a neutral position. Full rotation at the wrist/forearm; finger posture may vary.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: palm normal vector flipping from upward/neutral to downward — rotation event at wrist joint 0
action_library.notes: Contact_ratio typically low because this is a wrist-dominant motion with fingers usually extended or loosely curled

action_library.label: wrist_supination
action_library.description: Forearm rotating so the palm faces upward from a neutral or pronated position. Reverse of pronation.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: palm normal vector rotating to upward-facing — rotation event opposite direction from MAC_001
action_library.notes: Complement of MAC_001; both can appear in sequence as wrist oscillation (see MAC_011 wave)

action_library.label: wrist_flexion
action_library.description: Wrist bending toward the palm side (volar flexion); hand angle decreasing from the neutral aligned position.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: wrist angle event in palmar direction, change > 15 degrees
action_library.notes: Distinct from pronation/supination: this is a hinge motion in the flexion plane, not a rotation

action_library.label: wrist_extension
action_library.description: Wrist bending toward the back of the hand (dorsiflexion); hand angle increasing from the neutral aligned position.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: wrist angle event in dorsal direction, change > 15 degrees
action_library.notes: Complement of MAC_003

action_library.label: reach
action_library.description: Hand moving through space toward a target with fingers extended; wrist linear trajectory is the dominant signal. Pre-grasp approach phase.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: high wrist linear velocity > 0.3 m/s, low finger flexion ratio and variance
action_library.notes: Often precedes MAC_006 power_grasp or MIC_001 fingertip_pinch — sequence context helps confirm

action_library.label: power_grasp
action_library.description: Full-hand closure around an object; all fingers and thumb wrap around a cylindrical, spherical, or large target. Maximum contact area.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: simultaneous full flexion across all finger chains + thumb, palm-finger contact event
action_library.notes: Highest contact_ratio among single-hand macro classes due to full palm and finger contact with object

action_library.label: release
action_library.description: Full-hand opening from a closed grasp posture; all fingers extend simultaneously to release an object.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: simultaneous flexion ratio decrease from high (>0.6) to low (<0.2) across all fingers
action_library.notes: Temporal class — requires the transition from closed to open, not just an open-hand posture

action_library.label: transport
action_library.description: Hand moving through space while maintaining a closed grasp posture; object being carried from one location to another.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: high wrist linear velocity sustained over multiple frames, flexion ratio sustained > 0.5
action_library.notes: Distinguished from reach (MAC_005) by sustained high flexion during movement — fingers are closed, not extended

action_library.label: push
action_library.description: Palm or fingers applying force in the direction away from the body; hand decelerates at the contact point and may pause.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: wrist velocity toward target then deceleration event, palm-forward normal vector
action_library.notes: Contact_ratio rises at push contact moment then drops — the deceleration pattern is the primary signal

action_library.label: pull
action_library.description: Fingers or hand drawing an object toward the body; retraction trajectory after contact is established.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: wrist retraction velocity event after contact, flexion maintained during retraction
action_library.notes: Complement of MAC_009; distinguished by direction of wrist velocity vector relative to body centre

action_library.label: wave
action_library.description: Repetitive oscillating wrist rotation with extended fingers; social communicative gesture. Two or more oscillation cycles within the chunk.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: oscillating wrist rotation event repeated >= 2 times, low finger flexion ratio throughout
action_library.notes: contact_ratio near zero because fingers are extended and no contact is made; repetition count distinguishes from single MAC_001/002

action_library.label: static_hold_power
action_library.description: Hand maintaining a full-power grasp posture with minimal wrist movement for at least one second.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: low wrist linear velocity < 0.05 m/s, flexion ratio sustained > 0.5, stable contact_ratio
action_library.notes: Macro counterpart of MIC_014 — distinguished by high flexion (full grasp) vs precision finger posture

action_library.label: symmetric_mirror
action_library.description: Both hands performing the same movement simultaneously and symmetrically — e.g., both arms spreading outward or both fists closing at the same time.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: high inter-hand motion correlation coefficient (>0.7), symmetric wrist trajectories
action_library.notes: No direct inter-hand contact required — correlation of trajectories is the key signal

action_library.label: asymmetric_hold_act
action_library.description: Non-dominant hand stabilises or holds an object while the dominant hand performs fine manipulation on or around it. The most common bimanual task pattern in daily activities.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: non-dominant: low wrist velocity + high flexion; dominant: micro-movement signals active
action_library.notes: Requires velocity differential between hands — if both hands move equally, prefer BIM_008

action_library.label: handover
action_library.description: Object transferred from one hand to the other; both hands briefly in simultaneous contact with the object during the transfer phase.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: both hands converge spatially, simultaneous contact event from both, then diverge
action_library.notes: The convergence-contact-diverge temporal pattern is unique to this class

action_library.label: bimanual_reach
action_library.description: Both hands extending toward targets simultaneously, either to the same target or to two different targets in parallel. Low inter-hand contact.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: high wrist velocity both hands simultaneously, low flexion both hands, low contact_ratio
action_library.notes: Distinguished from BIM_001 symmetric_mirror by high velocity — this is a movement not a posture

action_library.label: clap
action_library.description: Both palms meeting and separating in a rapid, rhythmic pattern; inter-hand contact is full-palm and repeated.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: high inter-hand contact frequency, full-palm contact event symmetric, both wrists in mirror motion
action_library.notes: Highest contact_frequency among bimanual classes; if only one contact event occurs, prefer BIM_003 handover

action_library.label: two_hand_grasp
action_library.description: Both hands grasping the same large object simultaneously — e.g., holding a container, box, or tray with both hands wrapped around it.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: both hands sustained high flexion, sustained inter-hand spatial proximity, high contact_ratio
action_library.notes: Distinguished from BIM_007 finger_interlace by object-mediated vs direct hand-to-hand contact

action_library.label: finger_interlace
action_library.description: Fingers of both hands interleaved or clasped together; sustained multi-point direct inter-hand fingertip and mid-phalanx contact.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: multiple simultaneous fingertip-to-fingertip contact events from both hands, high contact duration
action_library.notes: Highest contact_ratio class in the entire library — near 1.0 is possible

action_library.label: bimanual_manipulation
action_library.description: Both hands acting on the same object with different roles and both also moving — e.g., opening a jar lid (one holds jar, one rotates lid), folding cloth, or assembling parts.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: both hands variable flexion over time, sustained inter-hand proximity, velocity differential between hands exists but both move
action_library.notes: Distinguished from BIM_002 by the fact that both hands are actively moving, not one static and one active

action_library.label: parallel_independent
action_library.description: Both hands performing completely different independent tasks simultaneously with no direct inter-hand interaction — e.g., left hand holds a phone while right hand writes.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: low inter-hand spatial correlation, different flexion patterns per hand, no inter-hand contact events
action_library.notes: Critical negative class — prevents the system from forcing an interaction label onto independent dual-hand activity

action_library.label: resting_neutral
action_library.description: Both hands in a neutral, unconstrained resting posture with no intentional movement. Baseline and idle state between actions.
action_library.handx_kinematic_signal: very low wrist linear velocity both hands (<0.02 m/s), low flexion variance, no contact events
action_library.notes: Anchor class for the low end of contact_ratio distribution. Essential for establishing a true baseline in evaluation
